title: Teaching the Western Union Band; Eddie Miller
summary: Of Netto's young students only one pianist went on; Eddie Miller came out of the two bands, and they discuss his name.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about these kids that you taught in the Western Union Band. Did any of them grow up to be professionals?

There was a boy, Martyr. He played piano in a couple of places. And to my knowledge, I don't think any of the others did. But then... Maurice took the item band. In fact, the item wanted me to take the band. I said, no. I said, one of them is driving me crazy. I said, I ain't going to get another one. So Maurice took it. And he happened to get Eddie Miller. So Eddie Miller was the product out of those two bands.
Well how did you pronounce Eddie Miller's name then?

Yeah, now, but it used to be Mula, Mala. I didn't know that. Some German guy told me that. He met him and it turned out his name was a German name. I think when he was in America it became Miller. Yeah, well he was hit from here.
